To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the plutonium contamination of the Black Sea was caused by the accident at Chernobyl NPP in 1986 and the main plutonium reservoirs are bottom sediments.
the 239, 240Pu concentrations in the Black Sea water and sediment samples were measured in the period 2000-2014.
239+240 Pu were found in the water column and bottom sediments in the Black Sea.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the radioecological model for Pu in the Black Sea.
the distribution and migration of 237,238Pu in the abiotic components of Black Sea ecosystems during post-Chernoblyl period.
the study of 239+24Pu distribution and migration in abiotic components during the post-Cherynobyl period.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
plutonium is a good indicator of the Black Sea ecosystem status and the main pathways of its contamination.
the plutonium migration within the Black Sea ecosystems is mainly governed by its accumulation in sediments.
the Black Sea ecosystems are not a source for the plutonium contamination in the adjacent marine environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
239,240 Pu is a very useful tool for tracing the migration of pollutants and their pathways through the Black Sea ecosystem.
plutonium is accumulated in the Black Sea bottom sediments and the sediments are the main plutonium depot in the Black Seas ecosystems.
the plutonium migration in the Black Sea is characterized by a high degree of its retention within the ecosystem and the plutonium biogoechemistry is similar to that of the 137Cs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
plutonium is a long-term contaminant in the Black Sea ecosystems, and it will remain there for a long time.
plutonium in the Black Sea is accumulated mainly in sediments and is characterized by the pedotropic behavior.
the plutonium isotope 239,240 Pu is a reliable indicator of the anthropogenic impact on the marine environment.
